tools.description: The latest published, non-prerelease, non-draft release of a repository with its release notes (Markdown body), tag, publish date, author and downloadable assets. found=false with release=null when the repository exists but has no published release.

Look up an npm package by name or pasted npmjs.com URL: what it is, who maintains it, which versions exist and which tag points where. Use `get_package_version` for one version's dependencies and tarball.

One package's current record: latest version and publish time, description, license, homepage/repository/issues links, keywords, version count, a download summary (npm and PyPI last week/month; crates.io last week/month/90 days/total; Maven Central publishes none) and a dependent count.
Chart or trend a package's downloads day by day; periods up to 18 months per request.
"Is lodash 4.17.15 vulnerable?", "what should I upgrade to": one package at a time. Use query_batch for a dependency list and vuln for the full record of one id.
See which versions of a package are actually installed this week (major-version adoption, whether a deprecated line is still in use).

One page of a repository's contributors ordered by commit count on the default branch, with login, account type and contribution count. Anonymous (email-only) contributors are not listed. GitHub refuses this listing for repositories with very large histories (for example torvalds/linux), which surfaces as an error naming the reason.

Exact issue counts for a repository (pull requests excluded, unlike the repository's open_issues_count): the total for the given state plus one count per requested label, from GitHub's issue search. Makes 1 + labels.length search requests; at most 5 labels per call because GitHub allows 10 keyless searches per minute per IP.

One page of a repository's issues filtered by state and labels (all given labels must match), sorted by created/updated/comments. Pull requests are excluded unless include_pull_requests is true, so a page may hold fewer than per_page records; pull_requests_excluded says how many were dropped. Each record carries title, state, labels, assignees, milestone, comment and reaction counts, body and timestamps.
The labels defined in a repository (name, color, description, whether GitHub-default), one page of up to 100. Use the names with issues and issue_counts.

One page of a repository's releases, newest first, including pre-releases and drafts visible to the public, each with tag, name, notes body, publish date and assets. Paginate with page/per_page; has_next says whether another page exists.
